## Design

### 2026-11-03: So I started out doing some research on these types of calculators. What i found is that for an 8 bit adders, you need 8 one bit adders. simple math. and a 1 bit adder needs 9 NOR gates. now in concep

**1.5h**

So I started out doing some research on these types of calculators. What i found is that for an 8 bit adders, you need 8 one bit adders. simple math. and a 1 bit adder needs 9 NOR gates. now in concept, NOR gates are super easy. Do an OR and flip it. Except with just transistors, it looks like this:

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 232653](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5EWBwlE4sonQmfnJte8X5LrEfrhjWaIo/0a1184753b0bbbab6da99a0de0c9835ffafbddac33978fd7519478619bebd9a8.png)

The little tail hanging underneath the first resistor connects to the other NOR gates (you'll see them in a bit). The tails hanging off R2 and R3 also connect to the other gates.
The first step is to get the other gates onto the screen with Ctrl-D.

Here's what it looked like:

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 232904](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5EWBwlE4sonQmfnJte8X5LrEfrhjWaIo/aeea98577ca0e89574b4a778b1cb85d39747c700b87ad0957ac3a92f87388244.png)

It looks simple now, but when we connect everything up, it gets messy ( and I didn't organize it to make wires as short as possible so its really messy):

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 235647](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5EWBwlE4sonQmfnJte8X5LrEfrhjWaIo/ea8d18c9ffe5c15d4058c20c279025d90fd00a4e6358775edc06cb79535d68f3.png)

This isn't verified yet, I'm gonna check it tomorrow.
